idiom_name: NULL pointer as the absent case plus explicit count- or sentinel-driven loops
implementation_notes: C has no sum type for absence; a pointer is documented as usable to implement optional types via the null pointer value, and every reader must test for NULL before dereferencing, because dereferencing a null pointer is undefined behaviour. The plural half of the traversal is a hand-written loop over an array whose length is tracked separately (count field) or by a sentinel, with the update applied through the pointer or the index; there is no generic traversal or optic, so each structure type gets its own get/update functions. Keep those functions beside the type and pair them with an explicit length so the zero-target case is a loop that never runs rather than an out-of-bounds read.
pitfalls: Every dereference needs a null check; a missed one is undefined behaviour, not a caught error, and the compiler cannot warn about it in general code.
Arrays do not carry their length: mixing count-based and sentinel-based conventions, or passing only the pointer, makes the zero-target case read past the array instead of doing nothing.
Accessors that hand out interior pointers live no longer than the struct they point into; freeing or reallocating the owner leaves a dangling pointer and ownership stays with the caller.
